W1.name: representation
W1.rule_restated: the representation cannot alter the frozen production semantics, acceptance criteria, length ladder or measurement definitions

a_adopted_rows_draining_front.what: per layer a Vec of adopted K rows and one of V rows plus a base; after appending p, drain every row below HistoryRange.required_start(p)
a_adopted_rows_draining_front.view: KvView::rows_from(base, …) — the static Rows backing (V2's fast path)
a_adopted_rows_draining_front.row_data_copied_per_append: none: the backend's row is adopted, as row/v1 does
a_adopted_rows_draining_front.release: each dropped row's own allocation freed as it is drained — witnessable on allocation identity (address + adoption generation)
a_adopted_rows_draining_front.cost: a memmove of ≈ w row pointers (24 B each, ≈24 KB) per sliding layer per append

b_adopted_rows_in_a_ring.what: VecDeque of adopted rows; pop_front is O(1)
b_adopted_rows_in_a_ring.view: a VecDeque is not contiguous, and rows(&self) cannot make_contiguous; needs a Dyn KvRows wrapper (dynamic dispatch per row read)

c_contiguous_ring_of_copied_rows.what: w rows × kv_dim preallocated per sliding layer; each appended row copied into its slot, the incoming Vec freed
c_contiguous_ring_of_copied_rows.view: wraps around, so not linear from base: Dyn or a two-segment view
c_contiguous_ring_of_copied_rows.row_data_copied_per_append: one row (the store traffic canonical/v1 pays)
c_contiguous_ring_of_copied_rows.complexity: largest: wrap-around indexing, and full-span layers still need a growing store

W1.decision: (a) adopted rows with a draining front
W1.reason: the smallest representation that meets every frozen condition: exact base/end, physical release of each dropped row witnessable on its own allocation identity, no second authority, zero row-data copies, and the static Rows view backing. (b)'s O(1) removal saves a pointer memmove that is a secondary cost, at the price of dynamic dispatch on every row read; (c) adds a copy per append and wrap-around indexing. Their allocator and throughput differences are secondary observations and are not measured as a comparison here.
W1.not_the_proof_provider: (a) shares the SHAPE of VIEW-1 V4's ExactRetention, which was a test instrument; window/v1 is written fresh as production code in larql-kv (vindex3/window.rs), with its own identity, factory and documentation, and without the proof provider's check log or seeding hooks
W1.identity_and_regions: identity `window/v1`, registered in shipped_continuations beside row/v1 and canonical/v1; declares ONLY the Kv region, so a plan needing Recurrent or LatentKv is refused at selection (frozen scope)
W1.fixed_representation_capacity_declared: per layer, the two row-list (Vec<Vec<f32>>) buffers: on a sliding layer their length never exceeds w + 1 (the appended row before the drain), so after warm-up their capacity stops growing — the only provider-born storage; every row allocation is adopted. W3 checks post-window growth of sliding-layer live K/V bytes against exactly this.
W1.full_span_layers: HistoryRange::Full: base stays 0 and nothing is drained — identical storage behaviour to row/v1

W2.name: provider
W2.result: window/v1 is exact, bounded by the plan authority, physically drops expired adopted rows, resumes correctly from non-zero base, and does not alter defaults.
what_landed: crates/larql-kv/src/vindex3/window.rs: WindowKvState (identity window/v1) and WindowFactory (regions: Kv only), written fresh as production code — no check log, no seeding hooks

registry.rs: shipped_continuations registers window/v1 beside row/v1 and canonical/v1; larql run reaches it with --continuation window/v1 (the CLI's registry starts from shipped_continuations); defaults unchanged (larql serve: canonical/v1; larql run: row/v1)
the C3 name ban (larql-vindex tests/continuation_closure.rs) now bans WindowKvState outside its own module, so PLUGIN-1 F2 covers the new built-in
W2.behaviour: per layer the backend's rows are adopted (never copied); after appending p every row below HistoryRange.required_start(p) is drained, its allocation dropped; a sliding layer holds w rows (w + 1 only between push and drain); a full-span layer never drains; lent through KvView::rows_from

witnesses.crates/larql-kv/src/vindex3/tests/window: shipped, and a hybrid plan is refused at selection by capability; base == required_start(p), end == p + 1, at most w rows held, rows adopted (the lent row IS the appended allocation) and every held absolute position reads back its own row, after every append; bit-identical to row/v1 through prefill, resumed prefill and decode on the sliding fixture with the sliding layer holding exactly its window; a sealed handoff filled until the sliding layer drained resumes with its base intact, decodes bit-identically to an uninterrupted row/v1 run, keeps advancing its base, and a second such handoff is refused under row/v1's authority
witnesses.S3: unchanged and still passing: VIEW-1 V4's seeded retention bug in the MEM-1 harness is refused before any kernel; no hooks were added to window/v1 for it

verdicts.exactness: HELD — logits digests bit-identical to row/v1 at every rung and every phase (batched prefill, resumed prefill, decode); the fixture witness test holds it on the sliding fixture
verdicts.bounded_retention: HELD — sliding-layer retained rows are exactly min(n, 1,024) at every rung (512, 1,024, then 1,024 at 1,124 / 2,048 / 4,096 / 8,192); full layers hold n under both providers. The per-append rule (base == required_start after every append) is asserted on the fixtures by the W2 tests and enforced at every step by the executor's construction-time required_range check; the gemma ladder adjudicates each rung's end state
verdicts.real_deallocation: HELD on allocation identity — every adopted row that fell below base was freed while that adoption was the live one: 2,900 / 29,696 / 89,088 / 207,872 rows at 1,124 / 2,048 / 4,096 / 8,192, each with its K and V allocations released by pointer (2×); every held row is still its live adoption; 0 unclassified append events. row/v1 control: nothing below base, every held row live
verdicts.scaling_law: HELD — sliding-layer live K/V 243.3 MB at every rung from 1,024 through 8,192 (row/v1 linear: 243.3 → 486.5 → 973.1 → 1,946.2 MB); no post-window growth beyond the declared fixed capacity, the per-layer row lists, which stay at 2.85 MB from 1,124 on while row/v1's grow to 11.4 MB
verdicts.global_layers_unchanged: HELD — full-span retained rows and K/V identical under both providers at every rung (21.0 → 335.5 MB)
verdicts.secondary_magnitude: as forecast: at 8,192 window/v1 sliding K/V 243.3 MB vs row/v1 1,946.2 MB (forecast ≈243 MB vs ≈1.95 GB) — 1.70 GB released

secondary_observations.time: window/v1 and row/v1 within noise of each other at every rung (8,192: 546 s vs 507 s) on a host under unrelated load (1-minute load 24.5 at start); recorded once, not re-run
secondary_observations.churn: appends and allocations in appends identical under both providers at every rung (68 allocations in appends at every rung, both); window/v1's frees in appends are exactly its evictions (2 per dropped row), row/v1 frees none
secondary_observations.memory: max RSS 15.6 GB, peak footprint 13.8 GB for the whole ladder process (model weights included); whole-process numbers, not the adjudicated subset
secondary_observations.correction: during the rehearsal a 124 MB 'peak footprint' was reported in conversation as heap; /usr/bin/time had wrapped cargo, so that figure was cargo's. The official run timed the test binary directly

closure.status: CLOSED 2026-09-27. This record is final; nothing in it changes after this entry.
closure.answer: Yes. At 8,192 logical positions, production continuation (window/v1) retains only the 1,024 positions the sliding-attention plan can still read, physically releases the other 7,168 positions as their original allocations, reduces sliding-layer K/V from 1.95 GB to 243 MB, and produces bit-identical output.
